newsitem.title: USA: U.S. studies further cuts in nuclear warheads.
newsitem.headline: U.S. studies further cuts in nuclear warheads.

text.p: The Clinton administration is studying the possibility of seeking an agreement with Russia on the outlines of a treaty requiring new cuts in strategic nuclear arms, the Washington Post reported on Thursday.
Quoting unidentified senior U.S. officials, the newspaper said the cuts would go well beyond the roughly 50 percent reduction set as a 10-year goal by U.S. and Russian leaders in 1993.

A secret Defence Department study was now examining the military consequences of ordering as many as 1,000 to 1,500 additional nuclear warheads to be scrapped on both sides, according to the report. That could leave residual forces of as few as 2,000 weapons, about the level of the U.S. nuclear arsenal in 1956.

Proposing new cuts was seen by some U.S. officials as a way to persuade Russian legislators to ratify the Start II treaty, which calls for the 50 percent reduction, the Post said. Moscow has balked at the accord on the grounds that it will cost too much to implement.
The Defence Department study was being conducted by the Joint Chiefs of Staff and by civilian experts at the Pentagon as part of a broader review of military strategy and budgets, the Post reported.
It was expected to be finished before a scheduled March summit meeting in Washington between President Clinton and Russian President Boris Yeltsin.
